chapter_text:
CHAPTER 2 — प्रेरणा (PRERANA)

Introduction — प्रेरणा किम्?

The word प्रेरणा (preranā) comes from the Sanskrit root प्रेरय् (√ईर् with the prefix प्र), meaning "to impel, to urge forward, to inspire". प्रेरणा is therefore the inner force that moves a person to noble action — inspiration and motivation. It is the spark that makes a student sit down to study, a farmer rise before dawn, and an ordinary person attempt something great. In this lesson (NIOS Secondary Sanskrit, Course 209) we ask a simple question: what inspires human beings to noble effort and to perseverance? We answer it through four famous public-domain Sanskrit verses — from the Ramayana, from Bhartrhari's नीतिशतक, and from the हितोपदेश — study their word meanings (शब्दार्थ), translate them into simple English, draw out their morals, and use them to learn a little Sanskrit grammar (व्याकरणम्).

Why प्रेरणा matters (प्रेरणायाः महत्त्वम्)

Talent and intelligence alone do not build a life; प्रेरणा does. A boat needs not only good wood but also a rower who wants to row. The Sanskrit tradition of नीति (practical wisdom) teaches again and again that the greatest strength a person can possess is not wealth, birth, or even cleverness, but उत्साह (enthusiasm/zeal) joined to उद्यम (steady effort). Enthusiasm without effort fades into day-dreaming; effort without enthusiasm becomes dull drudgery. True प्रेरणा unites the two — it lights the fire of उत्साह and keeps it burning through उद्यम, even when विघ्न (obstacles) come. The verses below were memorised by students for centuries precisely because a single line, recalled at a weak moment, can turn discouragement back into determination. They teach that success is not the gift of fate alone but the fruit of inspired, persevering work. The stories of great achievers, in India and elsewhere, are almost never stories of easy talent; they are stories of people who kept going. A scientist repeats an experiment a hundred times, a runner trains through pain, a student revises a hard chapter again and again — each is sustained not by luck but by प्रेरणा. This is why the Sanskrit teachers placed such verses at the very start of a child's moral education: to plant, early and deep, the conviction that one's own उत्साह and उद्यम, and not one's stars, shape one's future.

Four verses on प्रेरणा (शब्दार्थ सहित)

1) उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम् ।
   सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम् ॥
   (श्रीमद्वाल्मीकिरामायणम् — Valmiki Ramayana, public domain)
   शब्दार्थ: उत्साहः = enthusiasm, zeal, energy; बलवान् = powerful, strong; आर्य = O noble one (address); नास्ति = there is not; उत्साहात् = than enthusiasm (ablative, 'than'); परम् = higher, greater; बलम् = strength; सोत्साहस्य = of one who possesses enthusiasm (स + उत्साह); हि = indeed; लोकेषु = in the worlds; न किञ्चित् अपि = nothing at all; दुर्लभम् = difficult to obtain.
   Translation: Enthusiasm is powerful, O noble one; there is no strength greater than enthusiasm. Indeed, for one who is full of enthusiasm, nothing at all in the (three) worlds is hard to attain.
   Theme / Moral: उत्साह (enthusiasm) is the mightiest power. The zealous, self-motivated person can accomplish what seems impossible — प्रेरणा itself is strength.

2) प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
   प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः ।
   विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
   प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति ॥
   (भर्तृहरि-नीतिशतकम् — Bhartrhari, Niti Shataka, public domain)
   शब्दार्थ: प्रारभ्यते = is begun; न खलु = certainly not; विघ्नभयेन = through fear of obstacles (instrumental); नीचैः = by the low / inferior people; प्रारभ्य = having begun; विघ्नविहताः = struck down by obstacles; विरमन्ति = they stop, desist; मध्याः = the middling ones; विघ्नैः = by obstacles (instrumental plural); पुनः पुनः अपि = again and again; प्रतिहन्यमानाः = being struck back repeatedly; प्रारब्धम् = that which has been begun; उत्तमजनाः = the best / noblest people; न परित्यजन्ति = do not abandon.
   Translation: Inferior people never even begin a task, for fear of obstacles. Middling people begin, but stop the moment obstacles strike them. But the noblest, though struck by obstacles again and again, never abandon what they have once begun.
   Theme / Moral: The heart of प्रेरणा is perseverance. Anyone can feel enthusiasm for a moment; greatness lies in not giving up when विघ्न come again and again.

3) न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः ।
   अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति ॥
   (हितोपदेशः — Hitopadesha, public domain)
   शब्दार्थ: न = not; दैवम् = fate, destiny; अपि = even; सञ्चिन्त्य = having reflected upon; त्यजेत् = should abandon; उद्यमम् = effort, exertion; आत्मनः = one's own (genitive); अनुद्यमेन = without effort (instrumental); कः = who; तैलम् = oil; तिलेभ्यः = from sesame seeds (ablative plural); प्राप्तुम् = to obtain; अर्हति = is able, deserves.
   Translation: One should not abandon one's own effort even after reflecting on fate; for without effort, who is able to obtain oil from sesame seeds?
   Theme / Moral: प्रेरणा means never surrendering to "it is my fate". Just as oil comes from sesame only when it is pressed, results come only through उद्यम (effort) — not by waiting on दैव (destiny) alone.

4) उत्साहसम्पन्नमदीर्घसूत्रं
   क्रियाविधिज्ञं व्यसनेष्वसक्तम् ।
   शूरं कृतज्ञं दृढसौहृदं च
   लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति वासहेतोः ॥
   (हितोपदेशः — Hitopadesha, public domain)
   शब्दार्थ: उत्साहसम्पन्नम् = one endowed with enthusiasm; अदीर्घसूत्रम् = not a procrastinator (one who does not delay); क्रियाविधिज्ञम् = one who knows the right method of action; व्यसनेषु = in vices / addictions; असक्तम् = unattached, free; शूरम् = brave; कृतज्ञम् = grateful; दृढसौहृदम् = of firm friendship; च = and; लक्ष्मीः = Lakshmi, the goddess of fortune; स्वयम् = herself; वाञ्छति = desires, longs for; वासहेतोः = for the sake of dwelling (with him).
   Translation: A man who is full of enthusiasm, free of procrastination, skilled in the method of action, unattached to vices, brave, grateful and firm in friendship — Lakshmi (good fortune) herself longs to dwell with him.
   Theme / Moral: Fortune is not random; it is drawn to character. Enthusiasm joined to discipline, skill and integrity is the प्रेरणा that attracts lasting success.

व्याकरणम् — A little grammar from the verses (English explanation, Devanagari examples)

(A) सन्धि (Sandhi — the joining of sounds). When two sounds meet in Sanskrit they often combine and change. Three kinds appear in our verses:
  • दीर्घ-सन्धि (a short vowel + a like vowel → one long vowel): न + अस्ति → नास्ति (अ + अ = आ) "there is not".
  • गुण-सन्धि (अ/आ + उ/ऊ → ओ): स + उत्साहस्य → सोत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ) "of the enthusiastic one".
  • यण्-सन्धि (इ before a dissimilar vowel → य्): नास्ति + उत्साहात् → नास्त्युत्साहात् (the इ of नास्ति becomes य् before उ).
  • विसर्ग-सन्धि (अः before a soft consonant → ओ): उत्साहः + बलवान् → उत्साहो बलवान्.
  • व्यञ्जन-सन्धि (जश्त्व, त् → द् before a vowel/soft sound): त्यजेत् + उद्यमम् → त्यजेदुद्यमम्; and उद्यमम् + आत्मनः → उद्यममात्मनः.
Being able to SPLIT a joined form back into its parts (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is a key reading skill: e.g. सोत्साहस्य = स + उत्साहस्य, नास्त्युत्साहात् = नास्ति + उत्साहात्.

(B) विभक्ति (Vibhakti — case endings). A Sanskrit noun changes its ending to show its role. Examples drawn from the verses:
  • प्रथमा (nominative, the subject): उत्साहः "enthusiasm", लक्ष्मीः "Lakshmi", उत्तमजनाः "the noble (plural)", मध्याः "the middling (plural)".
  • द्वितीया (accusative, the object): उद्यमम् "effort", तैलम् "oil", प्रारब्धम् "the begun task".
  • तृतीया (instrumental, "by/with"): विघ्नभयेन "through fear of obstacles", विघ्नैः "by obstacles" (plural), अनुद्यमेन "without effort".
  • पञ्चमी (ablative, "from/than"): उत्साहात् "than enthusiasm", तिलेभ्यः "from sesame seeds" (plural).
  • षष्ठी (genitive, "of"): आत्मनः "of oneself", सोत्साहस्य "of the enthusiastic one".
  • सप्तमी (locative, "in/at"): लोकेषु "in the worlds" (plural), व्यसनेषु "in vices" (plural).

(C) धातुरूप (conjugation of a verb — worked example). The verb त्यज् ("to abandon"; भ्वादिगण, परस्मैपद) gives the form परित्यजन्ति ("they abandon") and त्यजेत् ("one should abandon") in our verses. Its लट् लकार (present tense) runs:
  प्रथमपुरुष: त्यजति (he abandons), त्यजतः (the two abandon), त्यजन्ति (they abandon).
  मध्यमपुरुष: त्यजसि, त्यजथः, त्यजथ.
  उत्तमपुरुष: त्यजामि, त्यजावः, त्यजामः.
Notice परित्यजन्ति is प्रथमपुरुष बहुवचन (third person plural) with the prefix परि-, exactly the त्यजन्ति form above.

SUMMARY (सारांश)

In this chapter you learned that प्रेरणा (from प्र + √ईर्, "to impel") is inspiration and motivation — the inner force that moves us to noble action and keeps us going through difficulty. You read four famous public-domain verses: उत्साहो बलवान् (from the Ramayana) on enthusiasm as the greatest strength; प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन (from Bhartrhari) on perseverance and never abandoning a begun task; न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य (from the Hitopadesha) on preferring self-effort to reliance on fate; and उत्साहसम्पन्नम् (from the Hitopadesha) on the disciplined character that fortune itself desires. For each you studied the शब्दार्थ, an English translation, and the moral. Finally you drew grammar from the verses — दीर्घ, गुण, यण् and विसर्ग सन्धि (and how to split them), the six common विभक्ति case-endings with examples, and the धातुरूप of त्यज् in लट् लकार. Memorise a verse or two; recalled at the right moment, they can turn discouragement back into determination.

chapter_summary.title: प्रेरणा (Prerana) — Chapter Summary
chapter_summary.intro: This is the NIOS Secondary Sanskrit (209) summary for Chapter 2. It explains what प्रेरणा (inspiration/motivation) is and why it matters, presents four famous public-domain verses on enthusiasm, perseverance and self-effort with their meanings and morals, and draws simple grammar — सन्धि, विभक्ति and धातुरूप — from the verses.

sections.heading: What प्रेरणा is and why it matters
bullets: प्रेरणा (from प्र + √ईर्, 'to impel') is inspiration/motivation — the inner force that moves a person to noble action.
It unites उत्साह (enthusiasm) with उद्यम (steady effort); enthusiasm alone fades, and effort alone is dull.
A single verse recalled at a weak moment can turn discouragement back into determination, which is why these verses were memorised for centuries.

sections.heading: Enthusiasm and self-effort
bullets: उत्साहो बलवान् (Ramayana): enthusiasm is the greatest strength — for the zealous, nothing is hard to attain.
न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य (Hitopadesha): do not abandon effort by blaming fate — oil comes from sesame only when pressed.
उत्साहसम्पन्नम् (Hitopadesha): fortune (Lakshmi) longs to dwell with the enthusiastic, disciplined, brave and grateful person.
Together they teach that success is inspired, persevering work — not the gift of chance.

sections.heading: Perseverance despite obstacles
bullets: Bhartrhari's प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन ranks people in three kinds by how they face विघ्न (obstacles).
नीचाः (the low) never begin for fear; मध्याः (the middling) begin but stop when obstacles strike.
उत्तमजनाः (the noblest) never abandon a begun task, though struck again and again — this is true प्रेरणा.

sections.heading: Sandhi from the verses
bullets: दीर्घ-सन्धि: न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ).
गुण-सन्धि: स + उत्साहस्य = सोत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ).
यण्-सन्धि: नास्ति + उत्साहात् = नास्त्युत्साहात् (इ → य् before उ); विसर्ग: उत्साहः + बलवान् = उत्साहो बलवान्.
सन्धि-विच्छेद (splitting a joined form back into its words) is a key reading skill.

sections.heading: Vibhakti and dhaturupa
bullets: प्रथमा (subject): उत्साहः, लक्ष्मीः; द्वितीया (object): उद्यमम्, तैलम्.
तृतीया 'by' विघ्नैः/अनुद्यमेन; पञ्चमी 'from/than' उत्साहात्/तिलेभ्यः; षष्ठी 'of' आत्मनः.
धातुरूप of त्यज् (लट्, प्रथमपुरुष): त्यजति / त्यजतः / त्यजन्ति — the verse's परित्यजन्ति is its plural.

key_takeaways: प्रेरणा (प्र + √ईर्) is inspiration/motivation — the inner force that moves us to noble, persevering action.
Enthusiasm is the greatest strength — उत्साहो बलवान् नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्.
Never abandon a begun task despite obstacles — the mark of उत्तमजनाः (Bhartrhari).
Do not surrender to fate; effort brings results — अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति.
Fortune favours the enthusiastic, disciplined and grateful — लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति.
गुण-सन्धि merges अ + उ into ओ (सोत्साहस्य); यण्-सन्धि turns इ into य् before a dissimilar vowel (नास्त्युत्साहात्).
विभक्ति endings show a word's role: पञ्चमी 'than/from' (उत्साहात्), सप्तमी 'in' (लोकेषु), तृतीया 'by' (विघ्नैः).

glossary.definition: Inspiration or motivation (from प्र + √ईर्, 'to impel'); the inner force that moves a person to noble action and perseverance.
Enthusiasm, zeal, energy; described in the Ramayana verse as the greatest of all strengths.
Effort, exertion, industry; the steady work that turns enthusiasm into real results.
Strength or power; the verse says there is no बल greater than उत्साह.
An obstacle or hindrance; how a person faces विघ्न separates the low, the middling and the noble.
The best or noblest people; those who never abandon a task once begun, despite repeated obstacles.
Fate or destiny; the verses warn against giving up effort by blaming दैव alone.
Oil; used in the image 'oil from sesame' to show that results come only through effort.
Not a procrastinator; a quality of one whom fortune favours (हितोपदेश verse).
The goddess of fortune and prosperity; she 'herself desires' to dwell with the enthusiastic and disciplined.
The joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; e.g. गुण-सन्धि merges अ + उ into ओ (सोत्साहस्य).
The splitting of a sandhi form back into its separate words, e.g. नास्त्युत्साहात् = नास्ति + उत्साहात्.
A noun's case ending, showing its role: प्रथमा (subject), द्वितीया (object), तृतीया (by), पञ्चमी (from/than), षष्ठी (of), सप्तमी (in).
The conjugation of a verb through persons and numbers, e.g. त्यज् in लट्: त्यजति / त्यजतः / त्यजन्ति.
A grateful person; one of the qualities that, with enthusiasm and bravery, attracts fortune.

worksheet.title: Worksheet — प्रेरणा (NIOS Sanskrit 209, Chapter 2)
worksheet.instructions: Attempt all questions. Write Sanskrit words in Devanagari and give your explanations in English. Refer to the verses in the lesson where needed.

questions.question:
Translate the following verse into simple English:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
questions.answer: Enthusiasm (उत्साह) is powerful, O noble one; there is no strength (बल) greater than enthusiasm. Indeed, for one who is full of enthusiasm (सोत्साह), nothing at all in the worlds (लोकेषु) is difficult to attain.
questions.explanation: Enthusiasm is the greatest power; the zealous can achieve anything.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ (English word meaning) of each: उत्साहः, बलम्, विघ्नः, उद्यमः, दुर्लभम्.
questions.answer: उत्साहः = enthusiasm/zeal; बलम् = strength; विघ्नः = obstacle; उद्यमः = effort; दुर्लभम् = hard to obtain.
questions.explanation: Core vocabulary from the chapter's verses.

questions.question: In one or two sentences, state the moral of 'न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः; अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति'.
questions.answer: One should not give up one's own effort by blaming fate. Just as oil (तैल) comes from sesame seeds only when they are pressed, results come only through effort (उद्यम) — not by waiting on destiny.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद (split) of: (a) नास्त्युत्साहात् (b) सोत्साहस्य.
questions.answer: (a) नास्त्युत्साहात् = नास्ति + उत्साहात् (इ → य् before उ, यण्-सन्धि). (b) सोत्साहस्य = स + उत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).
questions.explanation: Splitting a joined form back into its words is सन्धि-विच्छेद.

questions.question: State the विभक्ति (case) and its meaning-role for each: उत्साहात्, लोकेषु.
questions.answer: उत्साहात् = पञ्चमी (ablative) → 'than/from enthusiasm'. लोकेषु = सप्तमी (locative), plural → 'in the worlds'.
questions.explanation: पञ्चमी shows source/comparison, सप्तमी shows place.

questions.question: Explain the theme of perseverance using Bhartrhari's verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति'. How can a student practise this idea today?
questions.answer:
The verse ranks people into three kinds by how they face obstacles (विघ्न). The low (नीचाः) never even begin a task, out of fear of obstacles. The middling (मध्याः) begin, but stop the moment obstacles strike them. But the noblest (उत्तमजनाः), though struck by obstacles again and again (पुनः पुनः), never abandon (न परित्यजन्ति) what they have once begun. The theme is perseverance — true प्रेरणा is not a momentary thrill but the strength to keep going.
A student can practise this by not giving up after failing a test, by continuing a difficult project despite setbacks, by revising a hard chapter again and again, and by treating each obstacle as a step rather than a wall. Belonging to the उत्तमजनाः is a choice made daily through steady effort.
questions.explanation: Three kinds of people; perseverance of the noble; practical application.

questions.question: Write three simple Sanskrit sentences (in Devanagari) about the value of enthusiasm and effort (उत्साह / उद्यम). Give their English meaning.
questions.answer:
1. उत्साहेन कार्याणि सिध्यन्ति। (By enthusiasm, tasks are accomplished.)
2. उद्यमः एव जयस्य कारणम्। (Effort alone is the cause of victory.)
3. छात्रः विघ्नान् जित्वा नित्यं पठति। (The student, having conquered obstacles, studies every day.)
Together these say: we should work with enthusiasm, make steady effort, and overcome obstacles — for that is true प्रेरणा.
questions.explanation: Simple sentences using chapter vocabulary; verbs सिध्यन्ति, अस्ति (कारणम्), पठति.

questions.question: Translate 'नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्' and name the moral in one phrase.
questions.answer: 'There is no strength greater than enthusiasm.' Moral in one phrase: enthusiasm (उत्साह) is the greatest power.

questions.question: According to 'उत्साहसम्पन्नम्...लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति', name three qualities that attract fortune.
questions.answer: Any three of: उत्साहसम्पन्न (full of enthusiasm), अदीर्घसूत्र (free of procrastination), क्रियाविधिज्ञ (skilled in method), व्यसनेषु असक्त (free from vices), शूर (brave), कृतज्ञ (grateful), दृढसौहृद (firm in friendship).
questions.explanation: Lakshmi favours enthusiasm joined to discipline and integrity.

questions.question: What is प्रेरणा, and give two reasons why it is important?
questions.answer: प्रेरणा (from प्र + √ईर्, 'to impel') is inspiration or motivation — the inner force that moves a person to noble action. Two reasons it is important: (1) talent and intelligence achieve nothing without the will to act, which प्रेरणा supplies; (2) it unites उत्साह (enthusiasm) with उद्यम (effort) and keeps a person going through obstacles until success is reached.

questions.question: According to the chapter, why is प्रेरणा more important than talent alone?
questions.answer: Talent and intelligence achieve nothing without the will to act. प्रेरणा supplies that will — it unites उत्साह (enthusiasm) with उद्यम (effort) and keeps a person working through obstacles until success is reached. A boat needs not only good wood but a rower who wants to row.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'उत्साहो बलवान्' in one sentence.
questions.answer: It means 'enthusiasm (उत्साह) is powerful (बलवान्)' — that is, zeal and energy are themselves a great strength.

questions.question: Explain the message of Bhartrhari's verse 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः...'.
questions.answer: The verse divides people into three kinds by how they meet obstacles (विघ्न). The low (नीचाः) never begin a task, fearing obstacles. The middling (मध्याः) begin but stop when obstacles strike. The noblest (उत्तमजनाः), though struck again and again, never abandon what they have begun. The message: true greatness is perseverance.
questions.explanation: Three kinds of people; perseverance of the noble.

questions.question: Explain the meaning of 'अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति'.
questions.answer: It means 'without effort, who can obtain oil from sesame seeds?' Just as sesame yields oil only when pressed, no worthwhile result comes without उद्यम (effort).
questions.explanation: Image of oil from sesame; effort brings results.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: उत्साहः, बलम्, दुर्लभम्.
questions.answer: उत्साहः = enthusiasm; बलम् = strength; दुर्लभम् = hard to attain.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: विघ्नः, उद्यमः, दैवम्.
questions.answer: विघ्नः = obstacle; उद्यमः = effort; दैवम् = fate/destiny.
questions.explanation: Vocabulary from the perseverance and effort verses.

questions.question: Give the शब्दार्थ of: शूरम्, कृतज्ञम्, वाञ्छति.
questions.answer: शूरम् = brave; कृतज्ञम् = grateful; वाञ्छति = (she/he) desires.

questions.question: State and briefly explain the moral of 'उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्'.
questions.answer: The moral is that enthusiasm (उत्साह) is the greatest of all strengths — there is no बल greater than it. A person full of zeal finds nothing in the world hard to attain, because inner motivation drives one to overcome every difficulty. प्रेरणा itself is power.

questions.question: What lesson do the three types नीचाः, मध्याः and उत्तमजनाः teach us?
questions.answer: They teach that our worth is shown by how we face obstacles: the low never try, the middling give up when troubled, and the noble persevere to the end. We should aim to be उत्तमजनाः by never abandoning a good task once begun.

questions.question: A friend says 'my fate is bad, so I will not study'. Using 'न दैवमपि...', what should you advise?
questions.answer: I would say that the verse warns us not to give up effort even after thinking about fate: न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यमम्. Just as oil comes from sesame only when it is pressed, good results come only through उद्यम (effort). So my friend should keep studying with enthusiasm rather than blame destiny — effort, not fate, decides the outcome.
questions.explanation: Applies self-effort-over-fate to a real situation.

questions.question: Why does Lakshmi (fortune) favour the person described in 'उत्साहसम्पन्नम्...'?
questions.answer: Because that person combines enthusiasm with discipline and integrity — he is full of zeal, free of procrastination, skilled in method, free from vices, brave, grateful and firm in friendship. Fortune is drawn to such reliable character, not to luck; so Lakshmi 'herself desires' to dwell with him.

questions.question: Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of: (a) सोत्साहस्य (b) नास्त्युत्साहात्.
questions.answer: (a) सोत्साहस्य = स + उत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि). (b) नास्त्युत्साहात् = नास्ति + उत्साहात् (इ → य् before उ, यण्-सन्धि).

questions.question: Join by sandhi: (a) स + उत्साहस्य (b) त्यजेत् + उद्यमम्.
questions.answer: (a) स + उत्साहस्य = सोत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ). (b) त्यजेत् + उद्यमम् = त्यजेदुद्यमम् (त् → द्).

questions.question: What is गुण-सन्धि? Give one example from the verses.
questions.answer: गुण-सन्धि is the rule by which अ or आ meeting उ/ऊ becomes ओ (and meeting इ/ई becomes ए). Example from the verses: स + उत्साहस्य = सोत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ).

questions.question: Give the विभक्ति (case) and role of: (a) उत्साहात् (b) लोकेषु.
questions.answer: (a) उत्साहात् = पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'than/from enthusiasm'. (b) लोकेषु = सप्तमी (locative), plural — 'in the worlds'.

questions.question: Translate 'नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्' into English.
questions.answer: 'There is no strength greater than enthusiasm.' (उत्साहात् = than enthusiasm; परं बलं न अस्ति = there is no higher strength.)

questions.question: Translate the full verse 'न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः; अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति'.
questions.answer: 'One should not abandon one's own effort even after reflecting on fate; for without effort, who is able to obtain oil from sesame seeds?' It teaches that results come through effort, not by waiting on destiny.
questions.explanation: Full translation of the Hitopadesha verse.

questions.question: Which verse would you quote to inspire someone who gives up easily, and why?
questions.answer: I would quote Bhartrhari's 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः... प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति'. It teaches that the noblest never abandon a task, though struck by obstacles again and again — so one who gives up easily should choose to persevere like the उत्तमजनाः.

questions.question: What is प्रेरणा? Explain its meaning and its importance in life and in Sanskrit didactic (नीति) literature.
questions.answer:
प्रेरणा is 'inspiration' or 'motivation', formed from प्र (forward) + the root √ईर् (to move/impel) — literally the force that impels a person forward to noble action.
Its importance is great. First, talent and intelligence remain useless without the will to act, and प्रेरणा supplies that will. Second, it unites उत्साह (enthusiasm) with उद्यम (steady effort): enthusiasm alone fades into day-dreaming, and effort alone becomes dull drudgery, but together they carry a person to success. Third, प्रेरणा keeps one going through विघ्न (obstacles), so that a task begun is actually completed. In Sanskrit नीति and सुभाषित literature, verses on प्रेरणा were memorised for centuries because a single line recalled at a weak moment can turn discouragement back into determination. Thus प्रेरणा is treated as the true engine of a worthwhile life.
questions.explanation: Meaning by word-root + threefold importance + place in नीति literature.

questions.question: Take the verse 'उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्, सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्'. Give its word meanings and full explanation.
questions.answer:
शब्दार्थ: उत्साहः = enthusiasm/zeal; बलवान् = powerful; आर्य = O noble one; नास्ति = there is not; उत्साहात् = than enthusiasm; परम् = greater; बलम् = strength; सोत्साहस्य = of the enthusiastic one; हि = indeed; लोकेषु = in the worlds; न किञ्चित् अपि = nothing at all; दुर्लभम् = hard to attain.
Explanation: The verse (from the Ramayana) declares that enthusiasm is itself a great power, and that no strength — not wealth, birth, or even cleverness — is greater than it. The reason follows in the second line: for a person who is full of enthusiasm (सोत्साह), nothing in all the worlds is difficult to obtain, because inner zeal drives him to overcome every obstacle and to keep working until the goal is reached. The verse thus makes प्रेरणा (motivation) the foundation of all achievement: kindle उत्साह, and success follows.
questions.explanation: Word meanings + explanation of enthusiasm as supreme power.

questions.question: Discuss the theme of perseverance using Bhartrhari's 'प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन...' and explain how a student can practise it.
questions.answer:
Bhartrhari's verse ranks people into three kinds by how they face obstacles (विघ्न). The low (नीचाः) never even begin a task, paralysed by fear of obstacles. The middling (मध्याः) begin, but stop the moment obstacles strike them (विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति). The noblest (उत्तमजनाः), though struck by obstacles again and again (पुनः पुनः प्रतिहन्यमानाः), never abandon (न परित्यजन्ति) what they have once begun. The theme is that true प्रेरणा is not a momentary enthusiasm but the steadiness to keep going despite repeated setbacks.
A student can practise this in many ways: by not giving up after failing a test but analysing the mistake and trying again; by continuing a difficult project or a hard chapter even when progress is slow; by treating each obstacle as a step rather than a wall; and by finishing what is started instead of leaving things half-done. Choosing daily to persevere is what places one among the उत्तमजनाः. Thus the verse both inspires and gives a practical standard for character.
questions.explanation: Three kinds of people; perseverance; practical application.

questions.question: Write any TWO verses on प्रेरणा from the lesson in Devanagari and state the moral of each.
questions.answer:
1. उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्। सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥ — Moral: enthusiasm is the greatest strength; for the zealous, nothing is hard to attain.
2. न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः। अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति॥ — Moral: do not give up effort by blaming fate; results come only through effort, as oil comes from sesame only when pressed.
questions.explanation: Recall of two verses + their morals.

questions.question: Compare दैव (fate) and उद्यम (effort) as taught in this chapter.
questions.answer: The chapter sets दैव (fate) and उद्यम (effort) side by side and clearly favours उद्यम. The verse 'न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः' says one should not abandon one's own effort even after reflecting on fate. The image 'अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति' shows that just as sesame yields oil only when it is pressed, no result comes without effort — fate alone presses nothing. The Ramayana verse adds that enthusiasm (उत्साह), a form of उद्यम, is the greatest strength, and the Hitopadesha verse shows fortune itself favouring the diligent, not the idle. The teaching is not that fate does not exist, but that we must not use it as an excuse to stop trying: effort is in our hands, fate is not, so we should apply उद्यम and leave the rest.
questions.explanation: Contrast दैव vs उद्यम using the verses; effort is favoured.

questions.question: Translate the verse 'उत्साहसम्पन्नमदीर्घसूत्रं क्रियाविधिज्ञं व्यसनेष्वसक्तम्, शूरं कृतज्ञं दृढसौहृदं च लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति वासहेतोः' and explain it.
questions.answer:
Translation: 'A man who is full of enthusiasm, free of procrastination, skilled in the method of action, unattached to vices, brave, grateful, and firm in friendship — Lakshmi (fortune) herself longs to dwell with him.'
Explanation: The verse (from the Hitopadesha) lists seven qualities of character: उत्साह (enthusiasm), अदीर्घसूत्रता (no procrastination), क्रियाविधिज्ञता (knowing the right method), अव्यसनता (freedom from vices), शौर्य (bravery), कृतज्ञता (gratitude) and दृढसौहृद (firm friendship). It teaches that fortune is not a matter of luck but is drawn to disciplined, energetic and trustworthy character. The person who cultivates these qualities need not chase प्रेरणा or wealth — success comes to him by itself.
questions.explanation: Translation + explanation of the seven qualities that attract fortune.

questions.question: Explain सन्धि and सन्धि-विच्छेद with four examples taken from the verses of this chapter.
questions.answer:
सन्धि is the joining/merging of sounds where two words meet; सन्धि-विच्छेद is splitting such a joined form back into its separate words. Four examples from the verses:
1. न + अस्ति = नास्ति (अ + अ = आ, दीर्घ-सन्धि).
2. स + उत्साहस्य = सोत्साहस्य (अ + उ = ओ, गुण-सन्धि).
3. नास्ति + उत्साहात् = नास्त्युत्साहात् (इ → य् before उ, यण्-सन्धि).
4. उत्साहः + बलवान् = उत्साहो बलवान् (अः → ओ before a soft consonant, विसर्ग-सन्धि).
Being able both to join (सन्धि) and to split (सन्धि-विच्छेद) is essential for reading Sanskrit verses correctly.
questions.explanation: Definition + four worked examples with rules.

questions.question: Explain the common विभक्ति (cases) used in this chapter's verses with one example each, and give the धातुरूप of त्यज् in लट् लकार.
questions.answer:
Cases (with verse examples):
1. प्रथमा (nominative, subject): उत्साहः 'enthusiasm', लक्ष्मीः 'Lakshmi'.
2. द्वितीया (accusative, object): उद्यमम् 'effort', तैलम् 'oil'.
3. तृतीया (instrumental, 'by'): विघ्नैः 'by obstacles', अनुद्यमेन 'without effort'.
4. पञ्चमी (ablative, 'from/than'): उत्साहात् 'than enthusiasm', तिलेभ्यः 'from sesame seeds'.
5. षष्ठी (genitive, 'of'): आत्मनः 'of oneself', सोत्साहस्य 'of the enthusiastic one'.
6. सप्तमी (locative, 'in'): लोकेषु 'in the worlds', व्यसनेषु 'in vices'.
धातुरूप of त्यज् (लट् लकार, परस्मैपद): प्रथमपुरुष त्यजति / त्यजतः / त्यजन्ति; मध्यमपुरुष त्यजसि / त्यजथः / त्यजथ; उत्तमपुरुष त्यजामि / त्यजावः / त्यजामः.
questions.explanation: Six cases with examples + full present-tense conjugation of त्यज्.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
(a) What is described as powerful? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दुर्लभम्'. (c) In which विभक्ति is 'उत्साहात्'? (d) State the moral.
questions.answer: (a) Enthusiasm (उत्साह) is described as powerful (बलवान्). (b) दुर्लभम् = hard to attain. (c) उत्साहात् is पञ्चमी (ablative) — 'than enthusiasm'. (d) Moral: enthusiasm is the greatest strength; for the zealous, nothing is hard to attain.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: meaning, word, case and moral.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः।
विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति॥
(a) Who never begin a task? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'विघ्नैः'. (c) Who never abandon a begun task? (d) What is the lesson?
questions.answer: (a) The low (नीचाः) never begin, for fear of obstacles. (b) विघ्नैः = by obstacles (instrumental plural). (c) The noblest (उत्तमजनाः) never abandon a begun task. (d) Lesson: true greatness is perseverance — never give up despite repeated obstacles.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: three kinds of people and perseverance.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः।
अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति॥
(a) What should one not abandon? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'तैलम्'. (c) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'त्यजेदुद्यमम्'. (d) State the moral.
questions.answer: (a) One should not abandon one's own effort (उद्यम). (b) तैलम् = oil. (c) त्यजेदुद्यमम् = त्यजेत् + उद्यमम् (त् → द्). (d) Moral: do not blame fate and give up effort; results come only through उद्यम, as oil comes from sesame only when pressed.
questions.explanation: Comprehension with a sandhi split; self-effort over fate.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहसम्पन्नमदीर्घसूत्रं
क्रियाविधिज्ञं व्यसनेष्वसक्तम्।
शूरं कृतज्ञं दृढसौहृदं च
लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति वासहेतोः॥
(a) Whom does Lakshmi desire? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'कृतज्ञम्'. (c) What does 'अदीर्घसूत्रम्' mean? (d) What is the theme?
questions.answer: (a) Lakshmi desires the man who is enthusiastic, non-procrastinating, skilled in method, free of vices, brave, grateful and firm in friendship. (b) कृतज्ञम् = grateful. (c) अदीर्घसूत्रम् = not a procrastinator (one who does not delay). (d) Theme: fortune favours disciplined, energetic and trustworthy character, not luck.
questions.explanation: Comprehension: the qualities that attract fortune.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
(a) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'नास्त्युत्साहात्'. (b) Do the सन्धि-विच्छेद of 'सोत्साहस्य'. (c) Name the सन्धि type in each. (d) What quality does the verse praise?
questions.answer: (a) नास्त्युत्साहात् = नास्ति + उत्साहात्. (b) सोत्साहस्य = स + उत्साहस्य. (c) (a) is यण्-सन्धि (इ → य् before उ); (b) is गुण-सन्धि (अ + उ = ओ). (d) It praises उत्साह (enthusiasm) as the greatest strength.
questions.explanation: Comprehension focused on sandhi splitting and types.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः।
अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति॥
(a) In which विभक्ति is 'तिलेभ्यः'? (b) In which विभक्ति is 'आत्मनः'? (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'अनुद्यमेन'. (d) What is the message?
questions.answer: (a) तिलेभ्यः is पञ्चमी (ablative), plural — 'from sesame seeds'. (b) आत्मनः is षष्ठी (genitive) — 'of oneself'. (c) अनुद्यमेन = 'without effort'. (d) Message: effort, not fate, brings results — nothing (like oil from sesame) comes without exertion.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
न दैवमपि सञ्चिन्त्य त्यजेदुद्यममात्मनः।
अनुद्यमेन कस्तैलं तिलेभ्यः प्राप्तुमर्हति॥
(a) What image does the poet use? (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'उद्यमम्'. (c) What does 'सञ्चिन्त्य' mean? (d) What is the overall meaning?
questions.answer: (a) The image of obtaining oil from sesame seeds by pressing them. (b) उद्यमम् = effort. (c) सञ्चिन्त्य = 'having reflected/thought upon'. (d) Overall meaning: one should not give up effort by dwelling on fate, because results (like oil) come only through effort.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहो बलवानार्य नास्त्युत्साहात्परं बलम्।
सोत्साहस्य हि लोकेषु न किञ्चिदपि दुर्लभम्॥
(a) From which text is this verse taken? (b) What is its one-word central theme? (c) Complete: 'नास्त्युत्साहात् परं ____'. (d) For whom is nothing hard to attain?
questions.answer: (a) From the Ramayana (Valmiki). (b) उत्साह / enthusiasm (प्रेरणा). (c) बलम्. (d) For the enthusiastic person (सोत्साहस्य), nothing is hard to attain.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
उत्साहसम्पन्नमदीर्घसूत्रं
क्रियाविधिज्ञं व्यसनेष्वसक्तम्।
शूरं कृतज्ञं दृढसौहृदं च
लक्ष्मीः स्वयं वाञ्छति वासहेतोः॥
(a) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'शूरम्'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'दृढसौहृदम्'. (c) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'लक्ष्मीः'. (d) Name any two qualities the verse praises.
questions.answer: (a) शूरम् = brave. (b) दृढसौहृदम् = of firm friendship. (c) लक्ष्मीः = the goddess of fortune/prosperity. (d) Any two of: enthusiasm, non-procrastination, skill in method, freedom from vices, bravery, gratitude, firm friendship.

questions.question:
Read the verse and answer:
प्रारभ्यते न खलु विघ्नभयेन नीचैः
प्रारभ्य विघ्नविहता विरमन्ति मध्याः।
विघ्नैः पुनः पुनरपि प्रतिहन्यमानाः
प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति॥
(a) Translate 'प्रारब्धमुत्तमजना न परित्यजन्ति'. (b) Give the शब्दार्थ of 'विरमन्ति'. (c) What do the मध्याः do? (d) What is the moral?
questions.answer: (a) 'The noblest never abandon what they have begun.' (b) विरमन्ति = they stop/desist. (c) The middling (मध्याः) begin a task but stop when obstacles strike. (d) Moral: persevere to the end like the उत्तमजनाः; do not give up when obstacles come.
